step_matches.reason: Both have the Bureau/Office Chief initiating a purchase card for an employee (request/nominate).
Both have the nominee complete and sign Form A-498.
Both have the nominee complete GSA web-based purchase card training.
Both have the AO give the cardholder written authorization before the purchase.
Both have the cardholder confirm funds are available before purchasing.
Both have the cardholder complete and attach the Section 508 D&F form.
Both have the cardholder complete other forms the AO requires.
Both have the cardholder make or initiate the purchase with the card.
Both have the AO validate receipt and sign the receipt or invoice.
Both result in the accepting employee signing and dating the invoice, though golden frames it as the cardholder obtaining the signature.
AI S26 covers the cardholder reconciling and signing the SOA, merged with forwarding it to the AO.
Forwarding the SOA to the AO was merged into AI S26, which is already matched to S11.
Both have the AO review and sign the reconciled SOA.
Both have the AO forward the signed SOA to FOC RDG/TOG.
Both have the APC review card usage to find inactive accounts.
Both have the APC provide the inactive account list to each Bureau/Office.
Both have the Bureau/Office confirm the continued need for the inactive account.
Both have the APC suspend the inactive account until confirmation is received.
Both describe periodic or random reviews by the APC, auditors or OIG.
Both have the cardholder furnish documentation for the review.
Both have the cardholder review receipts for the questioned charge.
Both have the cardholder contact the merchant and document the actions taken.
Both have the cardholder submit a dispute to the contractor bank.
Both have the AO or Chief give the APC prior notice of the transfer or separation.
AI S49 covers providing records to the AO, merged with surrendering the card.
Card surrender was merged into AI S49, which is already matched to S25.
Both have the AO note on the final SOA that the departed cardholder could not sign it.
Both have the APC close the cardholder's account.
Both have the Chief designate a new AO and notify the APC in writing.

decision_matches.reason: Both check Section 508 coverage, and Yes leads to the 508 form in both; the No path proceeds onward despite slightly different step ordering.
Both check whether another employee accepted the goods, with Yes leading to the invoice signature and No to SOA reconciliation.
The AI embeds the 3-year inactivity criterion in step S38 and has no explicit decision for it.
Both check whether continued need is confirmed, with a negative answer leading to suspension and a positive one leading to no suspension.
Both check whether research confirms a dispute, with Yes leading to merchant contact and No to END.
Both check whether the merchant resolved the dispute, with Yes leading to END and No to a bank dispute.
Both check whether the cardholder left before the final SOA, with Yes leading to the AO note and No to account closure.
